newsitem.title: JAPAN: EPA says its view of economy no different from BOJ.
newsitem.headline: EPA says its view of economy no different from BOJ.

text.p: The view on the economy held by Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) does not differ much from that held by the Bank of Japan (BOJ), Japanese Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Friday.
"The government's view on the economy is becoming brighter. I don't think there is much difference between our view (and that of the BOJ)," he said.

Asked about the economic white paper's statement that firms and households needed to cope with the risk of a rise in interest rates, Aso said interest rate levels were an important factor in improving corporate structures.

The appropriate level for interest rates differs depending on the situation at each company, as the current recovery is patchy and varies between industries and according to the size of companies, he said.
"It is difficult for the EPA to say what interest rate level is appropriate," he said.
Aso pointed out, however, that Japan still needed to tackle structural reforms, despite better economic conditions, in order to strengthen its competitiveness in the global markets.

"Now is the time to rebuild the base for development by creating free and transparent markets and by pursuing structural reforms, as economic conditions are improving and Japan's economy has enough strength to carry out drastic reforms," he said.

The economic white paper released by the EPA earlier on Friday properly reflected current economic conditions and gave indications as to what is needed for the Japanese economy in the medium to long term, Aso said.

Asked about the slower recovery at smaller non-manufacturing firms compared with large manufacturers, he said there is no doubt that manufacturers are doing well, but those non-manufacturers that are sluggish are predominantly in the construction sector.
This was inevitable, he said, as public works spending has declined considerably.
He said the difference in the rate of recovery at various firms is no surprise in a free market economy such as Japan's.
There are some firms that may hinder the economic recovery, but there are others that are leading the economic recovery, he said.
"We must keep a careful watch over the economy," he said.
